en: The Glorious One Hundred and Eight-Name Hymn to Aṅgāraka (Mars)
The auspicious seed-mantra: Oṃ krāṃ krīṃ krauṃ saḥ, obeisance to Bhauma (Mars).
The son of Mahī, the highly fortunate Maṅgala, the bestower of auspiciousness;
the great hero, the great warrior, possessed of great strength and prowess. || 1 ||
He is most fierce and most auspicious, worthy of honor, and a source of compassion;
born of pride, he is intolerant and cruel, yet free from suffering and sin. || 2 ||
Supratīpa, Sutāmrākṣa, Subrahmaṇya, Sukhaprada; he who moves through crooked pillars and other obstacles, Vareṇya, Varada, and Sukhī. || 3 ||
Vīrabhadra, Virūpākṣa, Vidūrastha, Vibhāvasu;
he who moves through the circle of the constellations, the protector of the Kṣatriyas, yet devoid of the Kṣatriya nature. || 4 ||
Free from decay and growth, endowed with patience, and wise;
yielding inexhaustible fruit, he is within the range of vision and possesses auspicious marks. || 5 ||
Free from passion, free from fear, free from fever, the cause of all;
he whose movement is like that of the stars and constellations, the cutter away of various fears.

Desirable, the essence of compassion, adorned with shimmering golden ornaments, the destroyer of fear, the bestower of auspicious fruits, and the giver of the boon of fearlessness to his devotees. || 7 ||
A slayer of enemies, endowed with tranquility, a nurturer of those who seek refuge, courageous, a presiding lord of virtuous qualities, righteous, and invincible in battle. || 8 ||
Hari is far from the wicked, honored by the virtuous, the remover of all suffering, the restrainer of evil conduct, the shatterer of misery, and the one who is difficult to hold. 9.
The destroyer of bad dreams, the invincible, the liberator from the pride of the wicked;
born in the lineage of Bharadvāja, the son of the Earth, the ornament of the worthy. || 10 ||
Clad in red garments and possessing a red body, he is intent upon protecting his devotees;
four-armed and wielding a mace, he has a ram as his vehicle and is moderate in his diet.
He wields the spear and the trident, he is capable, and he is proficient in the science of weapons;
he is a logician, the support of the tamasic, an ascetic, and has copper-colored eyes.
Resembling molten gold, like the red filaments of a lotus, the tutelary deity of the lineage, who wanders amidst the cows and is adorned with virtues. || 13 ||
Aṅgāraka was born as Janārdana, the sovereign of the Avanti country;
he resides in the southern region of Sūrya and is a Yavana facing the southern direction.
Situated within the triangular mandala, he is praised by the lord of the thirty gods;
he is pure, the purifier, heroic, subject to purity, and the bringer of auspiciousness. 15.
The lord of the signs Aries and Scorpio is intelligent, measured in speech, a bestower of happiness, possessed of beautiful eyes, and the granter of all desired fruits. (16)
Thus ends the auspicious hymn of one hundred and eight names of Aṅgāraka.
